about: One case is one triage step. A finding was raised, somebody offered a reason it should not be reported, and the step is to say which of the rules in skills/ethical-hacker-squad/references/triage.md that reason invokes, what the answer to that rule is, and what follows for the finding. The answer is not in this file; it is in keys/, and scripts/gates/gate-triage-stage.sh checks that it stays there.
task: For the case below, name the triage rule the offered reason invokes, answer that rule from the closed vocabulary the rules file declares, and state what follows for the finding. Give the reason for the answer, naming the artifact it rests on.

finding.title: Report filter concatenated into SQL

finding.title: Archive name interpolated into a shell command
finding.detail: `backup.py` builds a `tar` command line by interpolation and runs it through a shell.

artifact.content:
import subprocess
import datetime

ARCHIVE_PREFIX = "nightly"          # module constant, never reassigned
RETENTION_DAYS = 14


def run_backup(data_dir):
    stamp = datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    cmd = f"tar -czf /var/backups/{ARCHIVE_PREFIX}-{stamp}.tgz {data_dir}"
    subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, check=True)


def prune():
    subprocess.run(
        f"find /var/backups -name '{ARCHIVE_PREFIX}-*.tgz' -mtime +{RETENTION_DAYS} -delete",
        shell=True, check=True)

from jobs.backup import run_backup, prune

# The only two call sites in the tree.
def nightly():
    run_backup("/srv/app/data")
    prune()

cases.exculpation_offered: The reviewer says the interpolated pieces never come from a request.
evidence_available: jobs/schedule.py, which holds the only call sites in the tree

finding.title: Workflow runs a third-party action from a moving reference

finding.title: Wildcard CORS on the API
finding.detail: The service returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so any origin can read responses from a credentialed API.

cases.exculpation_offered: The wildcard header is set inside the /healthz handler only, and that handler returns a fixed status document with no session data. Every other route returns without touching the header, so the wildcard never applies to a credentialed response.
evidence_available: api/app.py:12 sets the header inside healthz() and nowhere else
